title: POC weekly: catalog concordance & version fence discussion
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on choosing model variants from Redwood catalog, defining version pin strategy and escape/fallback plan. Reviewed benchmark trends, quantized vs fp16 tradeoffs, and security/deployment constraints. Agreed on an immediate benchmarking matrix and a canary rollback runbook to validate in staging.
topics: catalog comparison: baseline vs quantized variants
latency vs cost tradeoffs for inference profiles
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: ok hey everyone good to see you, thanks for joining. we are at our weekly sync for the poc with Aurelia. quick roll call?
[00:08] Carlos Mendes: hey Jordan, Simone, Rajiv, Leah here, all good.
[00:12] Priya Nair: hey all, Priya from Redwood. I'll drive the performance points today.
[00:17] Jordan Lee: awesome. quick agenda: review the last run results, catalog choices, discuss pinning/rollback policy and decide who runs the next benchmark. any additions?
[00:26] Simone Park: no, that's perfect. also want to talk about audit log retention for the private deploy.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: noted.
[00:34] Priya Nair: ok starting with results from last week's throughput test — we ran three candidates: rdl-3b (fp16), rdl-3b-q4_0 (quant), and rdl-7b-compat (downscaled). latency median: 78ms, 52ms, 110ms respectively under 50 concurrency steady-state. tokens per second was highest for the quant variant but saw slight coherency degradation on longer contexts.
[01:05] Carlos Mendes: when you say coherency degradation, is that hallucination count or answer drift?
[01:09] Priya Nair: mostly response drift on multi-turn prompts, subtle topical drift after 8–12 turns; hallucination metric stayed within our threshold. logs show parse-level fuzziness.
[01:20] Simone Park: that's the crux — our product needs high multi-turn fidelity for clinician workflows. we can't have drift after 6 interactions.
[01:27] Priya Nair: understood, so baseline rdl-3b fp16 keeps fidelity but higher cost. quant gives cost win but we risk small regressions.
[01:35] Jordan Lee: this is where version pinning and soft-fallbacks come in. recommended pattern: pin to rdl-3b fp16 in production, enable shadowing with rdl-3b-q4_0, and configure a soft fallback to the fp16 when similarity score drops below threshold.
[01:53] Rajiv Chopra: quick security question — if we shadow to a quantized model, are logs or KV cache items stored differently? any extra PII surface?
[02:02] Priya Nair: no difference in runtime storage; KV cache managed by the runtime and opaque — same retention and encryption policies apply. we'll use your KMS for key material in the private deployment.
[02:12] Leah Ortiz: and audit logs? we need 7 years retention per compliance. is that supported on Private?
[02:18] Jordan Lee: yes, Private supports configurable retention, we can push logs to your SIEM or S3 in the VPC. we'll share the integration doc.
[02:27] Carlos Mendes: ok good. can we dig into routing policies — what happens when we hit capacity on the dedicated pool?
[02:33] Priya Nair: we have smart routing options — region fallthrough, tiered model swap to cheaper variants, or queue based throttling. for this POC we recommend a priority routing: production traffic prefers fp16, if capacity constrained then route to quantized in the same region, with a hard cap to avoid quality cliffs.
[02:51] Simone Park: but that's risk — we don't want clinician experiences to suddenly degrade at 3pm when load spikes. is there a graceful degrade approach?
[02:58] Priya Nair: yes, soft-fallback. instead of directly switching to quant, we gate by a quality signal: if the last N responses fail similarity checks, route only query types with lower fidelity tolerance to the quant. also canary percentage ramp: 5%, 15%, 50%.
[03:13] Jordan Lee: let's walk through the rollback runbook we propose. Stage: run canary in staging for 48 hours with shadow logging. If similarity metric drops >2% or latency increases >20% on critical prompts, we auto-abort and pin back. For production rollout: 10% for 2 hours, review, then 40% for 4 hours, review. if any regression, immediate rollback and incident ticket.
[03:42] Carlos Mendes: who owns the cutoff thresholds? we need to agree.
[03:45] Priya Nair: we propose similarity threshold 0.92 (BLEU-ish score from our eval harness) and a latency SLO of p95 < 200ms. propose we iterate after the first canary.
[03:57] Simone Park: 0.92 seems reasonable as a starting point.
[04:00] Rajiv Chopra: also want explicit verification that fallback triggers don't leak metadata to the quant instance. is there any cross-instance data sharing?
[04:08] Priya Nair: no cross-instance exposure — requests are routed, logs are independently tagged. we can add a mandatory redaction step before any shadow payloads if you prefer.
[04:18] Leah Ortiz: added ask: can we keep the shadow payloads disabled by default until security signs off?
[04:23] Jordan Lee: absolutely.
[04:24] Priya Nair: ok switching to catalog concordance — we noticed your internal benchmarks favored a 4k context for clinician notes. rdl-3b variants are certified for up to 8k, but quantized variants had a small p95 penalty at 4k due to KV eviction patterns.
[04:41] Carlos Mendes: KV eviction patterns? can you explain briefly?
[04:44] Priya Nair: sure. quant kernels currently have slightly different memory footprints; under sustained 4k windows the KV cache churns more aggressively leading to extra recompute, so p95 spikes. it's patchable with new kernel selection or larger cache sizes; we'll recommend a cache size tweak in the config.
[04:58] Simone Park: that could be ok as long as it doesn't double our cost. what's the cost delta with increased cache?
[05:03] Priya Nair: small, maybe 8–12% on that route; still materially cheaper than full fp16 in many throughput scenarios. exact numbers will be in the spreadsheet.
[05:11] Jordan Lee: Priya will share the catalog comparison sheet showing latency/cost per 1M tokens for each variant and context length; that'll be our decision input.
[05:19] Priya Nair: yes, I'll attach the sheet. next, on pin semantics: we support three degrees — hard pin (force exact model version), soft pin (prefer model but allow fallback), and floating (use latest compatible). For Aurelia's prod, recommend hard pin to an fp16 build for first month, then soft pin to allow scheduled micro-updates after we validate.
[05:39] Carlos Mendes: timeline? we want to be in prod in ~6 weeks. is that feasible?
[05:44] Jordan Lee: feasible with 6-week runway: 2 weeks bench + safety tests, 2 weeks staging canary cycles, 2 weeks rollout and monitoring. depends on security signoff which could add time.
[05:52] Rajiv Chopra: security review can be parallelized; we'll start mapping evidence requests now.
[05:56] Simone Park: ok for benchmarking, who runs the 1M token cost/latency benchmark?
[06:00] Priya Nair: Redwood can run an end-to-end sim in our dedicated sandbox, but we'd prefer you run it too with real prompts. best is both — Redwood runs synthetic sim for capacity, Aurelia runs real prompts for fidelity.
[06:14] Jordan Lee: action — run combined benchmark: Redwood to run baseline sim by Thursday, Aurelia to run customer prompts in staging by next Monday.
[06:23] Leah Ortiz: note on staging: staging env is behind a separate VPC and must mimic the private deploy network egress to your KMS.
[06:30] Priya Nair: we have a staging template for Private that includes KMS routing and S3 log sinks; we'll provide Terraform snippets.
[06:38] Carlos Mendes: ok good. now let's record explicit next steps and owners.
[06:42] Jordan Lee: before we do that, any blockers we missed?
[06:45] Rajiv Chopra: one more — SOC 2 evidence for encryption at rest across the pipeline. we need the whitepaper and possibly a SOC attestation.
[06:53] Jordan Lee: we'll share the security pack and SOC docs.
[06:56] Priya Nair: quick note on competitors — we ran a side benchmark against Anthropic Claude-lite on our cluster; it had slightly better multi-turn retention but worse latency; we can share cursory notes but not the full dataset.
[07:09] Carlos Mendes: curious — were there licensing or cost differences that matter?
[07:12] Priya Nair: yes, licensing differs; Redwood's pricing for dedicated is per-reserved GPU hour + usage; third parties sometimes have higher per-token rates or restrictive licensing. details in pricing doc.
[07:25] Jordan Lee: ok let's spell out next steps.
[07:28] Priya Nair: Next steps (verbal): Redwood to run synthetic 1M-token benchmark by 2026-09-10; Priya to share catalog comparison spreadsheet and recommended pin (rdl-3b fp16) by 2026-09-09; Jordan to share security pack and SOC2 artifacts by 2026-09-09; Aurelia to run customer prompt benchmark in staging by 2026-09-14; simulate canary in staging for 48 hours after Aurelia run.
[07:58] Simone Park: i'll own the staging run and will coordinate with Leah.
[08:02] Leah Ortiz: noted.
[08:04] Rajiv Chopra: i'll compile the evidence list and share by EOW.
[08:08] Jordan Lee: great. any final Qs?
[08:11] Carlos Mendes: none here, thanks everyone.
[08:14] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and add the runbook to the shared drive. meeting adjourned.
